issue.title: Scribe: auto-apply ready-for-triage label on created issues

llm_context.input_title: Scribe: auto-apply ready-for-triage label on created issues
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: Scribe creates new GitHub issues as part of its agent role, but the issues currently lack the mandatory `ready-for-triage` label, requiring manual intervention to enter the triage pipeline. This issue requires updating Scribe's issue creation logic to automatically apply the `ready-for-triage` label using Scribe's own GitHub App identity.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: Scribe's issue creation routine currently invokes GitHub API calls to create issues without including the `ready-for-triage` label argument or configuration in the creation request payload, and needs to be extended to supply this label.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect routeLabel and dispatch configuration
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect symbol routeLabel in internal/dispatch/router.go and DispatchConfig in internal/config/config.go to understand how labels and issues are currently handled during dispatch and creation.

step_by_step_plan.title: Update issue creation payload to include ready-for-triage
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the issue creation routine to automatically append the 'ready-for-triage' label in the creation request payload using Scribe's GitHub App identity.

step_by_step_plan.title: Write regression test for automatic label application
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a unit test in internal/dispatch/router_test.go verifying that newly created issues include the mandatory 'ready-for-triage' label in their creation parameters.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run test suite for verification
step_by_step_plan.description: Execute the package tests to ensure the new label is correctly applied and no existing routing or issue creation behavior is broken.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: A mechanism allowing automated bots or agents to act with their own dedicated installation token and permissions rather than relying on human or generic tokens.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Using dedicated app identities ensures proper audit trails, granular permission scoping, and prevents permission escalation bugs.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Scribe must apply the `ready-for-triage` label using its own newly minted `scribe` app identity instead of the triage agent's permissions.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Workflows triggered by specific labels or event states that automate the distribution and handling of incoming work items.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Properly labeling newly created issues ensures they instantly route into the correct automated queue without manual operator intervention.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Applying the `ready-for-triage` label automatically upon Scribe issue creation allows the triage pipeline to immediately process the issue.

common_pitfalls: Using the triage agent's app identity or token instead of Scribe's dedicated `scribe` role identity.
Forgetting to handle API errors if the label does not exist or if the app lacks label-writing permissions on the repository.
